interface.signature: def countOfNodes(graph: List[List[int]], n: int) -> int:

preconditions.description: The number of nodes n must be between 1 and 10^4 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(graph) == n and all(len(neighbors) >= 0 for neighbors in graph)
preconditions.description: The graph is represented as an adjacency list with exactly n entries, where each entry is a list of neighbors (possibly empty).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for neighbors in graph for v in neighbors for u in range(1, n+1) if u == v or v in graph[u-1])
preconditions.description: The graph is undirected: if node u has neighbor v, then node v must have neighbor u. Node indices are 1-based and range from 1 to n.
The graph is connected and acyclic (tree), meaning it has exactly n-1 edges (each undirected edge counted twice in adjacency lists).

postconditions.expression: return_value == sum(1 for u in range(1, n+1) for v in range(u+1, n+1) if (distance(u, v) % 2 == 0))
postconditions.description: The function returns the count of unordered node pairs (u, v) where u < v and the shortest path distance between u and v is even. The distance is the number of edges in the unique path between u and v in the tree.
